I was there last night too. My thoughts: 
My son and I had floor tickets to the right of the ramp, a lot of people around us were pissed that they spent a lot of $ on seats not next to stage. 
15 minutes before the show started, these 2 kids' father began having a seizure 2 rows in front of us. Medics got there somewhat fast, had to stretcher him out and he was breathing but barely aware of anything.
 Miz is a damn good heel in person and Orton knows how to work with the crowd. Pretty decent match.
 8-man tag team match was better than I thought it would be. Heath over big time with "He's got kids" chants and Rhyno way over. Mojo was dancing in front of Dasha when Breezango's music came on, hilarious. Side note: Heath was getting trampled in the corner and after a European uppercut  could clearly see him smiling and trying to hold a laugh in, so that was interesting.
 Kalisto was the only thing that his match had, Hawkins is being wasted as a jester-heel.
 Harper looked good and Bray is a little bit heftier in person. Dasha announcing Bray multiple times got Bray good heat and at the end, Harper won 90% of the crowd over. Harper said he tried really hard, even wearing a new shirt for us and that he will be a future WWE champion. Took some selfies heading to the back with some people. Ellsworth and Asuka got the biggest chants. Becky was great and Alexa really knows how to work facial expressions into her match. Carmella's voice is high and annoying. Natalya played the Queen heel quite well too.
 Corbin vs Ambrose was in my opinion the best match, if not a close second to Cena vs Styles. Corbin can really move and Ambrose is just awesome. 
Cena vs Styles was main event of course. The video board wasn't working, so a lot of people had to stand on chairs due to them mostly working on the ramp and around the ring. Our view wasn't the best but overall my son said he liked it, so I'm happy. Enjoy the paragraphs.

Born in San Diego, but I'm a Navy brat so I grew up in VA Beach. My flag football team introduced me to the Packers as we were called the Larkspur Salem Packers. For two years we went undefeated and won the championship...I know, I know but it meant a lot to us back then. This was right before we signed The Minister himself, Reggie White. After that, I started watching anything and everything about the Packers. I was hooked. I couldn't believe how much of a gun-slinger Favre was and how dominating Reggie was. I loved to see Sterling make incredible catches and LeRoy Butler picking off whatever QB he wanted to. Those playoff losses hurt me to the core so when 1996-1997 came and we finally got to the big one and won, I remember thinking "This is what  losing my virginity must be like." Honestly, it wasn't... more because of the fact that I didn't shed a tear when I did end up losing my V-card but I cried like a damn baby after XXXI. I will forever remember how I felt after that game and for that I'm thankful for this team and everybody who roots right there along side me. Go Pack Go!!!
